source.title: From Narrow Unlearning to Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Erum Mushtaq; Anil Ramakrishna; Satyapriya Krishna; Sattvik Sahai; P. Goyal; Kai-Wei Chang; Tao Zhang; Rahul Gupta

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures overlap between RAI concept representations and relates it to emergent misalignment after refusal unlearning. It does not test feature superposition, polysemanticity, SAE feature properties, or the geometry of features competing for dimensions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal-rate changes after narrow refusal unlearning, but these are not outcomes predicted by the claim. Its representation-overlap analysis is related but measures similarity between RAI concept vectors, not superposition of sparse features. The two qualitative overlap findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Other refusal-score and MMLU results are left out because they do not measure the claim or its predicted behavior.
record.test_reason: The paper studies emergent misalignment after narrow refusal unlearning in Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B. Its representation analysis uses PCA concept vectors and cosine similarity between RAI concept vectors at layer 5. It never tests superposition, polysemantic neurons, capacity competition, SAE features or feature dimensionality. It does not even cite the superposition work; SAEs appear only in the limitations as future work. 'discusses' overstates the connection, so the relation is closer to cites_only (SAEs mentioned) or no engagement at all.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that narrow refusal unlearning lowers refusals on the target concept but induces emergent misalignment in other RAI domains, with Safety causing broader spillover than Cybersecurity. Adding retain-set cross-entropy largely, but not fully, restores refusals. Concept overlap in representation space correlates with how far the misalignment spreads. They also note that SAEs could give deeper insight.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses PCA-based concept vectors and cosine similarity to study RAI concept entanglement; it does not apply the Toy Models of Superposition method.

fits_no_version.finding: In Mistral-7B at layer 5, the Cybersecurity concept vector is more similar to Safety samples, and the Safety vector overlaps broadly with all other RAI concepts. This overlap pattern tracks the spread of emergent misalignment after unlearning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept entanglement measured by PCA concept-vector similarity in early layers correlates with cross-domain spillover (emergent misalignment) after narrow refusal unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The concept-overlap analysis is described as a simplistic training-free approach; the paper says larger models and more sophisticated techniques such as SAEs were not evaluated. The extracted text provides only qualitative descriptions of Figure 2, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not test the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Refusal-rate results in Tables 2–4 and MMLU results were not included because they measure outcomes of refusal unlearning, not superposition or its predicted behavior.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity transition and geometry: not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity: not studied.
Features spread across neurons, and SAE recovery of features in LLMs: not studied; SAEs are only mentioned as future work.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable and canonical units: not studied.
One-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features: not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The study is irrelevant to the superposition claim. The refusal-unlearning results (Tables 2–4) are rightly left out. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure makes features compete for neuron dimensions or causes important features to receive dedicated dimensions.
Polysemantic neurons and alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Feature distributions across neurons and SAE recovery of sparse features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical representational units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.check: The row measures cosine similarity between RAI concept vectors, not feature superposition, so it cannot show any version's effect. 'observed' should be cannot_determine relative to the claim. The baseline is not stated and the value is qualitative and figure-only.
